scoring.partial_credit: Award proportionally within each point. Citation credit is independent of substantive correctness.

substantive_logic_points.criterion: Explains that any CustomAuthScheme bypasses the ordinary pipeline; an exactly-generic scheme is rehydrated against immediate subclasses, a missing provider or falsey provider result raises, and an OAuth credential with auth_uri but no access_token is stored as exchanged_auth_credential and returns None; otherwise the provider credential returns directly.

Covers ordinary validation failures (missing raw OAuth/OIDC credential, missing oauth2 payload, and failed discovery for missing endpoints), discovery prerequisites/fill behavior, and the fast path that deep-copies only ready API_KEY/HTTP raw credentials.

States the source order: credential service when present, then context auth response; marks was_from_auth_response whenever that fallback is attempted; if still absent, deep-copies raw credentials for OAuth2 or configured OIDC client-credentials flow, otherwise returns None for user authorization.

Explains exchanger lookup; no-exchanger passthrough; synchronous service-account exchange; generic async exchange and its was_exchanged flag; refresh is skipped after any exchange and otherwise occurs only when a registered refresher says it is needed.

Explains that saving is attempted after auth-response fallback, exchange, or refresh; it is a no-op without a credential service; otherwise a deep-copied AuthConfig receives the final credential as exchanged_auth_credential and is saved, after which the final credential is returned.

citation_format_points.criterion: Material claims have inline `relative/path.py:start-end` citations that resolve at the frozen revision.
Citations cover the entrypoint plus the helper implementations actually used, rather than citing only the entrypoint declaration.

substantive_logic_points.criterion: Describes the copied invocation context with agent replaced, instrumentation scope, and order: before handling, optional early stop, core async generator under Aclosing, second early stop, then after handling.

Explains plugin callbacks run first and early-exit on first non-None; agent callbacks run only when plugin content is falsey, normalize singleton/list, accept sync or awaitable callbacks, and stop on first truthy content.

Distinguishes truthy before content (event includes content/actions and sets end_invocation), state-only delta (actions-only event without termination), and no result; notes run_async yields the before event before honoring termination.

Explains core events stream in order under Aclosing; an end_invocation set during core suppresses after callbacks; after callbacks have the same plugin-first/canonical fallback and sync/async handling, but truthy content does not set end_invocation, while state-only deltas still yield an event.

States that exceptions from before/core/after trigger on-agent-error notification and the original exception is re-raised; notification callbacks are best-effort across all plugins, and both per-plugin failures and even a manager/test-double failure are suppressed so they cannot mask the original.

citation_format_points.criterion: Material claims have inline `relative/path.py:start-end` citations that resolve at the frozen revision.
Citations cover both BaseAgent lifecycle helpers and PluginManager callback semantics.

substantive_logic_points.criterion: Explains that rewinds remove the rewind event and the range back through the earliest matching invocation, preserving chronological survivors; empty survivors, absent config, incomplete sliding config, insufficient new invocations, empty safe candidates, absent root agent, absent summarizer result, and related defensive checks yield nothing.

States token-threshold work is attempted first only when not skipped and fully configured; a successful token compaction returns immediately, while false/no-result falls through to sliding-window logic.

Explains that the token path uses latest observed prompt tokens or a character-based estimate, selects post-compaction candidates while retaining a tail and balancing calls, seeds from a prior summary when valid, and appends a produced event through session_service itself.

Explains the last compaction end timestamp, insertion-ordered unique invocation IDs with each ID's maximum timestamp, selection of IDs whose latest timestamp is newer, the interval threshold, and end ID as the last new invocation.

Explains start ID selection by backing up overlap_size from the first new ID with floor zero; slicing from the first start-ID event through the last end-ID event; removal of existing compaction events; and truncation to the longest balanced prefix.

Explains balanced-prefix bookkeeping: responses close before calls open within an event, calls plus requested confirmations/auth configs open obligations, and only the longest point with none open is safe; an existing summarizer is reused, otherwise only an LlmAgent can supply one, tracing invokes it with sliding_window, and a non-None result is yielded rather than appended here.

citation_format_points.criterion: Material claims have inline `relative/path.py:start-end` citations that resolve at the frozen revision.
Citations cover rewind filtering, arbitration, candidate safety, and summarization/persistence behavior.

substantive_logic_points.criterion: States the public async method delegates the blocking operation via asyncio.to_thread with user_id, filename, session_id, and version; app_name does not affect storage lookup.

Explains validated user/session path segments, user scope when session_id is absent or filename starts user:, otherwise session scope; user prefix stripping, Windows-separator normalization, rejection of absolute/escaping paths after resolution, and the empty/root-relative name fallback to artifact.

Explains numeric child-directory discovery with nonnumeric names ignored and sorted; missing artifact/no numeric versions return None; omitted version selects the greatest numeric version, while an unavailable explicit version returns None.

Explains missing or invalid metadata becomes None; the primary payload path is versions/<version>/<artifact-dir-name>; only when metadata has canonical_uri and the primary path is absent is a file:// URI converted and used, and only if its target exists.
States truthy metadata MIME type selects binary mode; missing payload returns None; otherwise bytes become inline_data with that MIME type and metadata display_name.

States absent/falsey MIME type selects text mode, including missing/corrupt metadata; missing payload returns None, otherwise UTF-8 text becomes Part(text=...). Notes that metadata alone does not make a missing payload loadable unless its usable file URI fallback exists.
